seek

seek(from: SeekFrom): IoResult<Offset>

Moves the position as from says: to an offset from the start, from the current position, or from the end of the file.

Seeking past the end is allowed; a later write there fills the gap with zeros. A position before the start of the file is an error. Seeking a stream that has no position (a pipe or a terminal) fails on POSIX and has platform-defined results on Windows.

Parameters

  • from — the origin and the offset from it

Returns

  • the new position, in bytes from the start of the file; an error when the File is closed, the resulting position would be negative (on POSIX, with is_invalid_input()), or the stream cannot seek

Example

var f = File.open(Path("data.bin")).value();
var length = f.seek(SeekFrom.End(0)).value();
f.seek(SeekFrom.Start(0));

seek_start

seek_start(pos: Offset): IoResult<Offset>

Moves the position to pos bytes from the start of the file, like seek(SeekFrom.Start(pos)) without allocating the SeekFrom.

Seeking past the end is allowed; a later write there fills the gap with zeros.

Parameters

  • pos — the new position, in bytes from the start

Returns

  • the new position, in bytes from the start of the file; an error as for seek

See also

  • seek

seek_end

seek_end(delta: Offset): IoResult<Offset>

Moves the position to delta bytes from the end of the file, like seek(SeekFrom.End(delta)). seek_end(0) moves to the end and returns the file's length.

Parameters

  • delta — the offset from the end of the file, in bytes; negative moves back from the end

Returns

  • the new position, in bytes from the start of the file; an error as for seek

See also

  • seek

seek_current

seek_current(delta: Offset): IoResult<Offset>

Moves the position by delta bytes from where it is, like seek(SeekFrom.Current(delta)). seek_current(0) returns the current position without moving it.

Parameters

  • delta — the offset from the current position, in bytes; negative moves back

Returns

  • the new position, in bytes from the start of the file; an error as for seek

See also

  • seek

seek

[Deprecated("use 'seek' with a 'SeekFrom' instead")] seek(offset: Offset, whence: int): IoResult<Offset>

Deprecated: use seek(SeekFrom) instead. Moves the position by offset relative to the origin whence.

Parameters

  • offset — the offset in bytes from the origin; may be negative
  • whence — the origin: 0 the start of the file, 1 the current position, 2 the end of the file

Returns

  • the new position, in bytes from the start of the file; an error as for seek(SeekFrom), or when whence is not 0, 1 or 2

set_length

set_length(size: ulong): IoResult<void>

Truncates or extends the file to exactly size bytes; bytes added are zeros. The position is kept, even when it is now past the end.

The File must have been opened for writing.

Parameters

  • size — the new length, in bytes

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when the File is closed, was not opened for writing, or the system refuses the size

set_len

[Deprecated("use 'set_length' instead", "set_length")] set_len(size: ulong): IoResult<void>

Deprecated: use set_length instead. Truncates or extends the file to exactly size bytes.

Parameters

  • size — the new length, in bytes

Returns

  • the same as set_length(size)

sync

sync(): IoResult<void>

Flushes the file's contents and metadata to the storage device, waiting until they are written (fsync on POSIX, FlushFileBuffers on Windows). Writes are already unbuffered in the process; this forces them out of the operating system's cache.

On Windows the File must have been opened with write access.

Returns

  • an Ok result once the data is durable; an error when the File is closed or the device reports a failure, or another platform error

lock

lock(): IoResult<void>

Takes an exclusive advisory lock on the whole file, waiting until no other holder has a lock on it, shared or exclusive. Modeled on Rust's File::lock.

The lock belongs to this File: another File opened on the same path (in this process or another) contends with it, and it is released by unlock, by close, or when the File is destroyed. Taking a lock while this File already holds one is platform-defined, as in Rust: POSIX converts the lock, Windows may wait forever. The lock is advisory on POSIX (flock(LOCK_EX)): it binds only those who also lock. On Windows (LockFileEx) it also stops other handles from reading or writing the file while held. The wait blocks the calling thread, also inside a task. WASI has no file locks.

Returns

  • an Ok result once the lock is held; an error when the File is closed, on WASI, or another platform error

See also

  • try_lock
  • unlock

Example

var f = OpenOptions().write(true).create(true).open(Path(".pep/fetch.lock")).value();
if (f.lock().is_ok()) {
    # ... work no other locker does at the same time ...
    f.unlock();
}

lock_shared

lock_shared(): IoResult<void>

Takes a shared advisory lock on the whole file, waiting until no other holder has an exclusive lock on it. Any number of Files can hold a shared lock at once. Modeled on Rust's File::lock_shared; otherwise as lock (flock(LOCK_SH) on POSIX, LockFileEx without LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK on Windows).

Returns

  • an Ok result once the lock is held; an error as for lock

See also

  • lock

try_lock

try_lock(): IoResult<bool>

Takes an exclusive advisory lock on the whole file if no other holder has a lock on it, without waiting. Modeled on Rust's File::try_lock; otherwise as lock.

Returns

  • true when the lock is now held, false when another holder has a lock on the file (Rust's TryLockError::WouldBlock); an error as for lock

See also

  • lock

Example

var held = f.try_lock();
if (held.is_ok() && !held.value()) {
    print("another process holds the lock\n");
}

try_lock_shared

try_lock_shared(): IoResult<bool>

Takes a shared advisory lock on the whole file if no other holder has an exclusive lock on it, without waiting. Modeled on Rust's File::try_lock_shared; otherwise as lock_shared.

Returns

  • true when the lock is now held, false when another holder has an exclusive lock on the file; an error as for lock

See also

  • lock_shared

unlock

unlock(): IoResult<void>

Releases the lock this File holds, shared or exclusive. Releasing a File that holds none is not an error. Closing or destroying the File releases its lock too. Modeled on Rust's File::unlock.

Returns

  • an Ok result once the lock is released; an error when the File is closed, on WASI, or another platform error

See also

  • lock

metadata

metadata(): IoResult<Metadata>

Queries the metadata of the open file itself (the target, when it was opened through a symlink): size, kind, read-only flag, permission bits and timestamps.

Returns

  • the file's Metadata; an error when the File is closed, or another platform error

Example

var size = f.metadata().value().size;

set_permissions

set_permissions(mode: Mode): IoResult<void>

Sets the permission bits of the open file (fchmod on POSIX).

mode holds the raw platform bits, as Metadata.permissions reports them: on POSIX the mode_t bits mode & 07777 (493, octal 755, for rwxr-xr-x). On Windows it is the FILE_ATTRIBUTE_* word, and only FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY (1) is applied; the File needs write access there. WASI has no permission bits, and this fails. set_read_only and set_executable change one property portably.

Parameters

  • mode — the new permission bits

Returns

  • an Ok result once they are set; an error when the File is closed, is_permission_denied() when the caller does not own the file (or on Windows the File was opened without write access), or another platform error

See also

  • Path.set_permissions

Example

var f = File.create(Path("run.sh")).value();
f.set_permissions(493);   # octal 755: rwxr-xr-x

set_read_only

set_read_only(read_only: bool): IoResult<void>

Makes the open file read-only, or writable again: the portable part of set_permissions.

On POSIX, read-only clears every write bit (octal 222), and writable sets only the owner's (octal 200), so a file never becomes writable by group or others this way. On Windows it sets or clears FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY, and the File needs write access. Fails on WASI, which has no permission bits.

Parameters

  • read_only — true to make the file read-only, false to make it writable by its owner

Returns

  • an Ok result once the file is changed; an error as for metadata() or set_permissions

See also

  • Metadata.read_only

set_executable

set_executable(executable: bool): IoResult<void>

Makes the open file executable, or not, without raw permission bits.

On POSIX, executable adds an execute bit for each class (owner, group, others) that may read the file, as chmod +x does with the usual umask; not executable clears all three. Windows has no execute bit (an extension such as .exe decides) and WASI no permission bits, so there this does nothing and succeeds.

Parameters

  • executable — true to make the file executable, false to stop it

Returns

  • an Ok result once the file is changed; an error as for metadata() or set_permissions

Example

var f = File.create(Path("run.sh")).value();
f.write_all("#!/bin/sh\necho hi\n");
f.set_executable(true);

set_modified

set_modified(time: long): IoResult<void>

Sets the open file's modification time, leaving its access time alone (futimens on POSIX, SetFileTime on Windows).

On Windows the File needs write access, and the time is kept to 100 ns. A later write to the file sets its modification time again, so call this after the last write.

Parameters

  • time — the new time, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, as Metadata.modified reports it

Returns

  • an Ok result once the time is set; an error when the File is closed, is_permission_denied() when the caller does not own the file (or on Windows the File was opened without write access), or another platform error

See also

  • Path.set_modified

set_accessed

set_accessed(time: long): IoResult<void>

Sets the open file's access time, leaving its modification time alone (futimens on POSIX, SetFileTime on Windows).

On Windows the File needs write access, and the time is kept to 100 ns.

Parameters

  • time — the new time, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, as Metadata.accessed reports it

Returns

  • an Ok result once the time is set; an error as for set_modified

See also

  • Path.set_accessed

close

close(): IoResult<void>

Closes the File now, to observe the error the system reports (for example a deferred write failure). Without it the destructor closes the handle and ignores errors.

Idempotent: closing a closed File succeeds. The File counts as closed afterwards even when closing reports an error, so the handle is never closed twice. A standard stream is only marked closed: the stream stays open, and File.stdout() and the like still work.

Returns

  • an Ok result on success or when already closed; the platform error when closing an owned handle fails

Example

var f = File.create(Path("out.bin")).value();
f.write_all("data");
if (f.close().is_err()) {
    return 1;
}

into_transfer

into_transfer(): FileTransfer

Moves the file's handle into a FileTransfer, which another thread takes with File.adopt, and leaves this File closed. A File is not thread-safe, so this is how a thread hands one to another, such as the pipe from a child process's standard output to the thread that reads it while this one writes to the child.

Returns

  • the token; for a closed File, one that adopt fails on

Example

import async;
import [File, Path] from io;

var transfer = File.open(Path("notes.txt")).value().into_transfer();
var reader = async.Thread.spawn(() => {
    var mine = File.adopt(transfer).value();
    var text = mine.read_all();
});
reader.join();

FileTransfer

[Shared] struct FileTransfer

A file's handle on its way from one thread to another: made by File.into_transfer, taken by File.adopt. Unlike a File, it is thread-safe, so a shared function (a body for async.spawn or Thread.spawn) can capture it and a Channel can carry it. If no one adopts it, the handle is closed when the last reference goes, unless it is one the File did not own (a standard stream).

Constructor

FileTransfer()

construct(handle: FileHandle, owned: bool)

Wraps a file handle. File.into_transfer makes these; use it.

Parameters

  • handle — the handle, or an invalid one for an empty token
  • owned — whether the File the token came from closed its handle

Directory

Source: runtime/io/directory.pep

DirEntry

struct DirEntry

One entry of a directory listing, as Directory.entries() returns it.

The kind flags come from the listing itself and describe the entry without following symlinks. On POSIX a symlink has is_symlink set and is_file and is_directory clear; on Windows a symlink or junction to a directory has both is_directory and is_symlink set. Entries that are none of these (a FIFO, socket or device on POSIX) have all three flags clear. Call metadata() for the details of what the entry points to.

Example

import io;

var list = io.Directory.open(io.Path("src")).value().entries().value();
ulong i = 0;
while (i < list.count) {
    if (list[i].is_file) {
        print(list[i].Name);
    }
    i = i + 1;
}

Fields

path

Path path

The entry's full path: the listed directory's path joined with name (relative when the directory's path was relative).

name

String name

The entry's own file name, without any directory part.

file_type

FileType file_type

The kind of the entry, without following symlinks: Symlink for a symlink (on Windows, any reparse point, even one to a directory), Other for anything that is not a file, directory or symlink.

is_file

bool is_file

Whether the entry is a regular file (never true for a symlink).

is_directory

bool is_directory

Whether the entry is a directory. On POSIX never true for a symlink; on Windows also true for a symlink or junction to a directory.

is_symlink

bool is_symlink

Whether the entry is a symlink (on Windows, any reparse point, junctions included), which is not followed.

Constructor

DirEntry()

construct()

Creates an empty entry: empty path and name, all kind flags false and file_type Other. Entries are normally obtained from Directory.entries().

Methods

metadata

metadata(): IoResult<Metadata>

Returns the metadata of the entry, following symlinks, exactly like Path.metadata() on the entry's path. The file system is queried again now, so the result reflects any change since the listing was read.

Returns

  • the entry's Metadata (of the target, for a symlink); an error when it cannot be stat'ed, with is_not_found() when the entry was removed since the listing or is a dangling symlink

See also

  • Path.metadata

Directory

struct Directory

A directory on the file system, identified by its path, together with static functions that create, remove and inspect directories and the process's current and temporary directories.

A Directory holds no operating-system handle: open only checks that the path is a directory, and each call to entries() reads the listing afresh.

Example

import io;

var dir = io.Directory.temp().join("scratch").join("logs");
if (io.Directory.create_all(dir).is_ok()) {
    var d = io.Directory.open(dir).value();
    var count = d.entries().value().count;
    io.Directory.remove_all(io.Directory.temp().join("scratch"));
}

Fields

path

Path path

The directory's path, as given to open.

Constructor

Directory()

construct()

Creates a Directory with an empty path, which names no directory. Use Directory.open to get one for an existing directory.

Static methods

open

static open(path: Path): IoResult<Directory>

Checks that path exists and is a directory (following symlinks) and returns a Directory for it. Nothing is kept open, so the directory can still be renamed or removed afterwards.

Parameters

  • path — the directory's path; a relative path is resolved against the current directory whenever the Directory is used

Returns

  • the Directory; an error when path cannot be stat'ed (is_not_found() for a missing or empty path, is_permission_denied()) or is not a directory (is_not_a_directory(), message "not a directory")

Example

import io;

var d = io.Directory.open(io.Path("src"));
if (d.is_err() && d.error().is_not_a_directory()) {
    print("src is a file");
}

create

static create(path: Path, mode: Mode = 511): IoResult<void>

Creates one directory (mkdir on POSIX, with mode less the umask; CreateDirectoryW on Windows). Its parent must already exist.

Giving the mode here means the directory never exists with another one. mode is the POSIX mode_t permission bits (448, octal 700, for a directory only its owner may use); it is ignored on Windows and WASI.

Parameters

  • path — the directory to create
  • mode — the permission bits on POSIX, less the umask; 511 (octal 777) by default

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when the directory cannot be created: is_already_exists() when anything (a file too) is already at path, is_not_found() when the parent is missing or the path is empty, is_permission_denied() when the parent is not writable

See also

  • create_all

Example

import io;

var keys = io.Directory.create(io.Path("keys"), mode = 448);   # octal 700

create_all

static create_all(path: Path, mode: Mode = 511): IoResult<void>

Creates a directory and any missing parents, like mkdir -p. Succeeds without doing anything when path is empty or already a directory (or a symlink to one). Parents are found lexically with Path.parent(); a relative path is created under the current directory. It is safe against another process creating the same directories at the same time.

mode applies to path itself when it is created, as mkdir -p -m does: missing parents get the default, 511 (octal 777) less the umask, so the new directory can always be made inside them. An existing directory keeps its mode. Ignored on Windows and WASI.

Parameters

  • path — the directory to create, with its parents
  • mode — the permission bits of path on POSIX, less the umask; 511 (octal 777) by default

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when a directory cannot be created: is_already_exists() when a file (not a directory) is at path or at one of its parents, is_permission_denied(), and so on. Parents created before the failure are left in place

Example

import io;

var r = io.Directory.create_all(io.Path("build").join("out").join("logs"));

symlink

static symlink(target: Path, link: Path): IoResult<void>

Creates a symbolic link at link that points to the directory target (symlink on POSIX; CreateSymbolicLinkW with SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_DIRECTORY on Windows). Use File.symlink for a link to a file: Windows makes the two kinds differently. POSIX makes the same link either way.

target is stored as given and need not exist; a relative target is resolved against the directory that holds the link, not the current directory. On Windows, making a symlink needs Developer Mode or an administrator, and fails with is_permission_denied() otherwise.

Parameters

  • target — the directory the link points to
  • link — where to create the link

Returns

  • an Ok result once the link exists; an error with is_already_exists() when something is already at link, is_not_found() when its parent is missing or a path is empty, is_permission_denied(), or another platform error

See also

  • Path.read_link

Example

import io;

io.Directory.symlink(io.Path("releases/1.2"), io.Path("current"));

remove

static remove(path: Path): IoResult<void>

Removes an empty directory (rmdir on POSIX, RemoveDirectoryW on Windows).

Parameters

  • path — the directory to remove; it must be empty

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when it cannot be removed: is_directory_not_empty() when it still has entries, is_not_found() when it is missing or the path is empty, is_not_a_directory() when path is a file, is_permission_denied()

See also

  • remove_all

remove_all

static remove_all(path: Path): IoResult<void>

Removes path and, if it is a directory, everything inside it, recursively. Symlinks are removed, never followed, so nothing outside the tree is touched. A file or symlink at path itself is simply removed.

Stops at the first failure, leaving whatever was not yet removed; on Windows a read-only file inside the tree is such a failure (is_permission_denied()).

Parameters

  • path — the file, symlink or directory tree to remove

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when something cannot be removed: is_not_found() when path does not exist (unlike rm -rf, a missing path is an error) or is empty, is_permission_denied(), and so on

See also

  • remove

Example

import io;

var tree = io.Directory.temp().join("my-scratch");
var r = io.Directory.remove_all(tree);
if (r.is_err() && !r.error().is_not_found()) {
    print(r.error().message);
}

current

static current(): IoResult<Path>

Returns the process's current directory, against which relative paths are resolved (getcwd on POSIX, GetCurrentDirectoryW on Windows).

Returns

  • the current directory as an absolute path; an error when it cannot be determined, such as is_not_found() on POSIX when the directory has been removed

See also

  • set_current

set_current

static set_current(path: Path): IoResult<void>

Changes the process's current directory (chdir on POSIX, SetCurrentDirectoryW on Windows). This affects the whole process, every thread included: relative paths used anywhere afterwards resolve against the new directory.

Parameters

  • path — the new current directory; a relative path is resolved against the old one

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when the directory cannot be entered: is_not_found() when it is missing or the path is empty, is_not_a_directory() when it is a file, is_permission_denied()

See also

  • current

temp

static temp(): Path

Returns the directory for temporary files. It is not created or checked, so it may not exist.

On POSIX it is $TMPDIR with any trailing / removed, or /tmp when TMPDIR is unset or empty (/data/local/tmp on Android, which has no /tmp; an app should use its cache directory instead). On Windows it is what GetTempPathW reports (from TMP, TEMP, USERPROFILE, or the Windows directory) with its trailing separator removed unless it is a root, or . if that call fails.

Returns

  • the temporary directory's path, never an error

Example

import io;

var scratch = io.Directory.temp().join("my-tool");

Methods

entries

entries(): IoResult<DirEntry[]>

Reads the directory's listing now, all at once: every entry except . and .., in the order the operating system returns them (not sorted). Uses opendir/readdir on POSIX and FindFirstFileW/FindNextFileW on Windows. To read the entries one at a time instead, loop over the Directory itself (see iterate).

Returns

  • the entries, possibly none; an error when the directory cannot be read: is_not_found() when it no longer exists (or, on POSIX, path is empty), is_permission_denied(), or on POSIX is_not_a_directory() when path now names a file

Example

import io;

var list = io.Directory.open(io.Path(".")).value().entries();
if (list.is_ok()) {
    var n = list.value().count;
}

iterate

iterate(): DirectoryIterator

Returns an iterator that reads the directory's listing one entry at a time, as for (var entry in dir) does, without building an array.

Each element is an IoResult<DirEntry>. The listing is opened by the first next(), so a directory that cannot be read yields one error (the same errors as entries()) and then ends; an error while reading also ends it. The entries come in the order the operating system returns them, without . and ... The listing is closed when it ends, or when the iterator is released, so leaving the loop early with break or return closes it too.

Returns

  • a new DirectoryIterator positioned before the first entry

Example

import io;

var dir = io.Directory.open(io.Path(".")).value();
for (var entry in dir) {
    if (entry.is_err()) {
        print(entry.error().message);
        break;
    }
    print(entry.value().name);
}

DirectoryIterator

struct DirectoryIterator

The iterator Directory.iterate() returns, and a for loop over a Directory drives: the directory's entries, read one at a time, each as an IoResult<DirEntry>.

It holds the open listing (a DIR* on POSIX, a find handle on Windows) from the first next() until the listing ends, an error ends it, or the iterator is released.

See also

  • Directory.iterate

Example

import io;

var it = io.Directory.open(io.Path(".")).value().iterate();
while (it.next()) {
    var entry = it.current();
}

Constructor

DirectoryIterator()

construct(path: Path)

Makes an iterator over the entries of the directory at path. Nothing is opened until the first next().

Parameters

  • path — the directory to list

Methods

next

next(): bool

Reads the next entry, opening the listing on the first call.

Once it returns false it keeps returning false.

Returns

  • true if there is a current element (an entry, or the error that ends the listing), false once the listing has ended

current

current(): IoResult<DirEntry>

Returns the element the last successful next() moved to.

Returns

  • the current entry, or the error that ended the listing

Panics

  • if next() was never called, or already returned false ("DirectoryIterator.current() without an entry")

Glob

Source: runtime/io/glob.pep

glob_matches

glob_matches(pattern: String, path: String): bool

Returns whether path matches the glob pattern as a whole.

The pattern language:

  • * matches any run of characters within one path component (never a /), the empty run included.
  • ? matches one character (a code point) other than /.
  • ** as a whole component matches zero or more components, so src/**/*.pep matches src/a.pep and src/x/y/a.pep. Elsewhere it is the same as *.
  • [abc] matches one of the characters listed, [a-z] one in the range, and [!abc] or [^abc] one not listed. A ] right after the [ (or the !) is listed rather than closing it.
  • {a,b} matches either alternative; alternatives may hold any pattern, braces included.

/ separates components in the pattern; on Windows \ in path counts as / too. There is no escape character, since it would clash with Windows separators: [*] matches a literal *. An unclosed [ or { matches itself, so every pattern is valid. Matching is case-sensitive, and * and ? match a leading . like any other character.

Parameters

  • pattern — the glob to match against
  • path — the path to test, as text

Returns

  • true when the whole of path matches

Example

import io;

var yes = io.glob_matches("src/**/*.{pep,md}", "src/io/glob.pep");   # true
var no = io.glob_matches("*.pep", "src/main.pep");                  # false: `*` stops at `/`

glob

glob(pattern: String): Path[]

Returns the existing paths that match the glob pattern, sorted and without duplicates. The pattern language is glob_matches's.

The walk starts at the longest leading run of components without *, ?, [ or {: src/**/*.pep lists only under src, and *.pep the current directory. A relative pattern gives relative paths. ** does not descend into symlinked directories, so a link cycle cannot loop; other components follow symlinks. Directories that cannot be read are skipped, and a pattern whose start does not exist matches nothing.

Parameters

  • pattern — the glob to expand

Returns

  • the matching paths, joined with the platform separator, sorted by their text; empty when nothing matches

Example

import io;

for (var source in io.glob("runtime/**/*.pep")) {
    print(source.to_string());
}

Source: runtime/io/watch.pep

ChangeKind

enum ChangeKind

What happened to a path, as a FileChange reports it.

Cases

Created

Created

The path was created, or moved into the tree.

Removed

Removed

The path was removed, or moved out of the tree.

Modified

Modified

The file's contents or attributes changed.

Overflow

Overflow

The system dropped changes because they came faster than they were read; the path is the watched directory. List it again to catch up.

FileChange

struct FileChange

One change Watcher.wait reports.

Fields

kind

const kind: ChangeKind

What happened.

path

const path: Path

The path that changed: the watched directory's path, as given to Watcher.open, joined with the path inside it.

Constructor

FileChange()

construct(kind: ChangeKind, path: Path)

Creates a change.

Parameters

  • kind — what happened
  • path — the path that changed

Watcher

[NotCopyable("owns an operating-system handle and cannot be copied; open another Watcher on the receiving thread")] struct Watcher

Watches a directory and everything below it for changes: files and directories created, removed, renamed or written.

wait() returns the next batch of changes, waiting until there is one. In a task (inside async.run) the wait parks only the task, and the task's cancel or timeout ends it; elsewhere it blocks the thread. A rename reports the old path Removed and the new one Created. One write may report Modified more than once, and consecutive repeats within a batch are dropped.

Each system watches its own way: inotify on Linux, with a watch on every directory of the tree (new ones are added as they appear, and what they already hold is reported Created); kqueue on macOS, which holds a descriptor for every directory and file, so a large tree may need a higher ulimit -n; ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows. Changes are recorded from open on, also while no wait is running. When the system drops changes, wait reports an Overflow change. A change made right as a new directory appears may be missed on Linux and macOS: look at the directory when its Created arrives if that matters. Watching is not supported on WASI.

Example

import io;

var watcher = io.Watcher.open(io.Path("src")).value();
while (true) {
    var changes = watcher.wait();
    if (changes.is_err()) {
        break;
    }
    for (var change in changes.value()) {
        print($"{change.kind.name()}: {change.path}");
    }
}

Network addresses

Network addresses: IpAddress (IPv4 or IPv6), SocketAddress (an IP address and a port), and resolve, which turns a host name into socket addresses.

Source: runtime/io/address.pep

IpAddress

struct IpAddress

An IPv4 or IPv6 address.

Make one with IpAddress.v4, IpAddress.v6, IpAddress.parse, or one of the well-known addresses (loopback_v4(), unspecified_v6(), ...). IpAddress() is the IPv4 unspecified address 0.0.0.0.

to_string() prints IPv4 in dotted decimal (127.0.0.1) and IPv6 in the RFC 5952 form (::1, 2001:db8::8a2e:370:7334); an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address prints as ::ffff:1.2.3.4. An IPv4 address and the IPv6 address that maps it are different values.

An IPv6 address can carry a scope id, the network interface a link-local address such as fe80::1 belongs to. Its text form is fe80::1%eth0 (RFC 4007), and a socket address carries it to the system as sin6_scope_id.

See also

  • SocketAddress

Example

import io;

var a = io.IpAddress.parse("192.168.1.10").value();
var b = io.IpAddress.v6(8193, 3512, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1);   # 2001:db8::1
print(a.is_v4());         # true
print(b.to_string());     # 2001:db8::1

parse

static parse(text: String): IoResult<IpAddress>

Parses an IPv4 address in dotted decimal (192.168.0.1) or an IPv6 address in the RFC 4291 text form (::1, fe80::1:2, ::ffff:10.0.0.1), with an optional scope (fe80::1%eth0).

IPv4 needs exactly four decimal parts from 0 to 255 without leading zeros. IPv6 takes up to eight groups of one to four hex digits (either case), at most one ::, and an optional IPv4 address as the last 32 bits. Brackets and surrounding spaces are not accepted.

An IPv6 address may end in % and a scope: a decimal scope id (%3), or the name of a network interface (%eth0), which is looked up on this machine (so it fails where there is no such interface).

Parameters

  • text — the address to parse

Returns

  • the address; an error with is_invalid_input() when text is not a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address or names an unknown interface

Example

var r = IpAddress.parse("10.0.0.300");
print(r.is_err());   # true: 300 is out of range
var scoped = IpAddress.parse("fe80::1%7").value();
print(scoped.scope_id());   # 7

A scope id follows as % and the name of its interface (fe80::1%eth0), or the number when no interface on this machine has that index (fe80::1%9).

SocketAddress

struct SocketAddress

An IP address and a port: where a socket is bound, or where it connects or sends.

Make one with SocketAddress(address, port) or SocketAddress.parse, or get a list from resolve. SocketAddress() is 0.0.0.0:0. The text form is address:port for IPv4 and [address]:port for IPv6.

See also

  • IpAddress
  • resolve

Example

import io;

var any = io.SocketAddress(io.IpAddress.unspecified_v4(), 8080);
var local = io.SocketAddress.parse("[::1]:443").value();
print(local.port());   # 443

resolve

resolve(host: String, port: u16): IoResult<SocketAddress[]>

Looks up the socket addresses of a host, with port attached to each.

A host that is already an IP address (as IpAddress.parse reads it) is returned as is, without a lookup. Anything else goes to the system resolver (getaddrinfo on POSIX, GetAddrInfoW on Windows), which consults the hosts file and DNS and blocks until it answers. The addresses come in the resolver's order of preference, IPv4 and IPv6 mixed, each at most once.

Parameters

  • host — a host name such as "example.com" or "localhost", or an IP address
  • port — the port to put in every result

Returns

  • at least one address; an error with is_not_found() when the name has no address, is_invalid_input() when host is empty, or another resolver error

Example

import io;

var r = io.resolve("localhost", 8080);
if (r.is_ok()) {
    for (var address in r.value()) {
        print(address.to_string());   # 127.0.0.1:8080, [::1]:8080, ...
    }
}

Sockets

TCP and UDP sockets: TcpListener accepts connections, TcpStream is one connection, UdpSocket sends and receives datagrams.

Every call blocks the calling thread until it completes (in a task, it parks only the task), or until the socket's read or write timeout expires. Addresses are SocketAddress values; resolve turns a host name into them.

Source: runtime/io/socket.pep

TcpListener

[NotCopyable("owns an operating-system socket and cannot be copied")] struct TcpListener

A TCP socket that listens for connections.

TcpListener.bind opens one on a local address; each accept() waits for the next connection and returns it as a TcpStream together with the peer's address. Binding to port 0 lets the system choose a free port; local_address() tells which.

On POSIX the listener sets SO_REUSEADDR, so a server can restart while connections from its previous run linger in TIME_WAIT. An IPv6 listener keeps the system's default for accepting IPv4 too (on Linux and macOS it does, on Windows it does not).

Closing: the destructor closes the socket when the last reference goes; close() closes it earlier and reports errors. Every operation on a closed listener fails with an error no IoError predicate identifies (EBADF on POSIX, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE on Windows).

See also

  • TcpStream

Example

import io;

var listener = io.TcpListener.bind(io.SocketAddress.parse("127.0.0.1:0").value()).value();
print(listener.local_address().value().to_string());   # 127.0.0.1:<port>
while (true) {
    var (stream, peer) = listener.accept().value();
    stream.write_all("hello " + peer.to_string());
}

Constructor

TcpListener()

construct()

Creates a closed listener: is_open() is false and every operation fails. Use TcpListener.bind to get an open one.

Static methods

bind

static bind(address: SocketAddress): IoResult<TcpListener>

Opens a TCP socket bound to address and starts listening on it.

Parameters

  • address — the local address to listen on: a specific interface (127.0.0.1:8080), every interface (0.0.0.0:8080, [::]:8080), or port 0 for any free port

Returns

  • the listening socket; an error with is_address_in_use() when another socket has the port, is_address_not_available() when the address is not one of this machine's, is_permission_denied() for a privileged port, or another platform error

Methods

is_open

is_open(): bool

Returns whether the listener is open.

Returns

  • false after close() and for a TcpListener() never bound

accept

accept(): IoResult<(TcpStream, SocketAddress)>

Waits for the next incoming connection and returns it.

Returns

  • the connected stream and the peer's address; an error when the listener is closed, or another platform error

incoming

incoming(): Incoming

Returns an iterator that accepts connections one at a time, for a for loop over incoming streams.

Each step waits in accept() and yields the connected stream, or the error accept() returned; an error does not end the iteration, so a server can log it and keep going, or break. The iteration ends once the listener is closed. Use accept() instead when the peer's address is needed.

Returns

  • a new Incoming positioned before the first connection

Example

import io;

var listener = io.TcpListener.bind(io.SocketAddress.parse("127.0.0.1:8080").value()).value();
for (var connection in listener.incoming()) {
    if (connection.is_err()) {
        print(connection.error().message);
        continue;
    }
    connection.value().write_all("hello");
}

local_address

local_address(): IoResult<SocketAddress>

Returns the address the listener is bound to, with the port the system chose when it was bound to port 0.

Returns

  • the local address; an error when the listener is closed, or another platform error

close

close(): IoResult<void>

Closes the listener now. Closing a closed listener does nothing. Connections already accepted stay open.

Returns

  • an Ok result on success or when already closed; the platform error when closing fails

Incoming

struct Incoming

The iterator TcpListener.incoming() returns: each connection the listener accepts, as an IoResult<TcpStream>.

next() waits for the next connection; an accept error is yielded as an item rather than ending the iteration. The iteration ends once the listener is closed. The iterator holds a reference to the listener, so the listener stays open while the iterator lives.

Constructor

Incoming()

Makes an iterator over the connections listener accepts.

Parameters

  • listener — the listener to accept on

Methods

next

next(): bool

Waits for the next connection.

Returns

  • true with the connection or the accept error as the current item; false once the listener is closed

current

current(): IoResult<TcpStream>

Returns the item the last successful next() moved to.

Returns

  • the accepted stream, or the error accepting it

Panics

  • if next() was never called or returned false ("Incoming.current() without a connection")

SharedTcpListener

[Shared] struct SharedTcpListener

A TCP listening socket that any thread can accept connections on: the thread-safe counterpart of TcpListener, for servers that accept on every worker of async.run at once (see async.spawn_on_each_worker). Each connection goes to one of the threads waiting in accept, and the stream it returns belongs to that thread.

A shared function may capture it. There is no close(), since another thread may be waiting on it: the socket closes when the last reference goes, which, for accept loops in tasks, is once async.run has cancelled them (accept then fails and the loop returns).

See also

  • TcpListener

Example

import async;
import io;

main(): int {
    async.run(() => {
        var listener = io.SharedTcpListener.bind(io.SocketAddress.parse("0.0.0.0:7000").value()).value();
        async.spawn_on_each_worker(() => {
            while (true) {
                var accepted = listener.accept();
                if (accepted.is_err()) {
                    return;
                }
                var (stream, peer) = accepted.value();
                stream.write_all("hello");
            }
        });
    });
    return 0;
}

Wraps a listening socket. Use SharedTcpListener.bind.

TcpStream

[NotCopyable("owns an operating-system socket and cannot be copied")] struct TcpStream

A TCP connection: a reliable, ordered stream of bytes in both directions.

Get one from TcpStream.connect (to an address), TcpStream.connect_host (to a host name) or TcpListener.accept. read appends what has arrived to a byte array and returns 0 once the peer has closed its side; write sends bytes.

Each call is one system call and blocks until it can make progress: a read returns as soon as some bytes are there, not when max bytes are, and a write may send fewer bytes than given. read_exact and write_all loop until done. Sending never raises SIGPIPE; writing to a connection the peer has closed fails with is_connection_reset().

Closing: the destructor closes the socket when the last reference goes; close() closes it earlier and reports errors. Every operation on a closed stream fails with an error no IoError predicate identifies (EBADF on POSIX, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE on Windows).

See also

  • TcpListener

Example

import io;

var stream = io.TcpStream.connect_host("example.com", 80).value();
stream.write_all("HEAD / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n");
var reply = Array<u8>();
while (stream.read(reply, 4096).value() > 0) {
}

Constructor

TcpStream()

construct()

Creates a closed stream: is_open() is false and every operation fails. Use TcpStream.connect or TcpListener.accept to get an open one.

Static methods

connect

static connect(address: SocketAddress): IoResult<TcpStream>

Opens a connection to address, waiting until it is established.

Parameters

  • address — the address to connect to

Returns

  • the connected stream; an error with is_connection_refused() when nothing listens there, is_timed_out() when the peer does not answer, or another platform error

connect_timeout

static connect_timeout(address: SocketAddress, milliseconds: ulong): IoResult<TcpStream>

Opens a connection to address like connect, but gives up with is_timed_out() when it is not established within milliseconds, instead of after the system's own limit (often minutes).

Parameters

  • address — the address to connect to
  • milliseconds — the longest wait, at most 4294967295 (about 49 days); 0 waits as long as connect does

Returns

  • the connected stream, with no read or write timeout; an error with is_timed_out() when the time runs out, is_invalid_input() when milliseconds is too large, or an error as for connect

Example

var r = TcpStream.connect_timeout(SocketAddress.parse("192.0.2.1:80").value(), 2000);
if (r.is_err() && r.error().is_timed_out()) {
    print("no answer within 2 seconds");
}

static connect_host(host: String, port: u16): IoResult<TcpStream>

Resolves host with resolve and connects to the first of its addresses that accepts, trying them in order.

Parameters

  • host — a host name or an IP address
  • port — the port to connect to

Returns

  • the connected stream; the error from resolve when the name has no address, or the error from the last address tried

Example

var r = TcpStream.connect_host("localhost", 8080);
if (r.is_err() && r.error().is_connection_refused()) {
    print("nothing is listening on 8080");
}

Returns

Waits until data arrives, then appends up to max bytes of it to buffer with a single system call, like File.read.

Reads until exactly count more bytes are appended to buffer.

Sends bytes from data with a single system call, waiting until the system can take at least some of them.

The send may be partial: it can send fewer than data.count bytes. Use write_all to send everything.

Returns

Sends all of data, repeating the send until every byte is sent.

Returns

Sends all of the UTF-8 bytes of text, as write_all(u8[]) does. No newline or terminator is added.

Closes the sending side of the connection: the peer's reads return 0 once it has read everything sent before. This side can still read.

Returns

set_no_delay

set_no_delay(enabled: bool): IoResult<void>

Turns Nagle's algorithm off (true) or on (false) with TCP_NODELAY. With it off, small writes go out at once instead of being held back to combine with later ones: lower latency for request/response traffic, more packets.

Parameters

  • enabled — true to send small writes immediately

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when the stream is closed, or another platform error

set_read_timeout

set_read_timeout(milliseconds: ulong): IoResult<void>

Limits how long a read waits: when no data arrives for milliseconds, the read fails with is_timed_out() and the stream stays open for another try. Each wait counts on its own, so a read_exact may take longer in all. 0, the default, waits as long as it takes. It works outside a task and in one, where the task's async.timeout can end the wait sooner.

Parameters

  • milliseconds — the longest wait, at most 4294967295 (about 49 days); 0 for none

Returns

  • an Ok result; an error with is_invalid_input() when milliseconds is too large, or an error when the stream is closed

Example

stream.set_read_timeout(5000);   # give up after 5 seconds of silence

Returns the read timeout set_read_timeout set.

Returns

set_write_timeout

set_write_timeout(milliseconds: ulong): IoResult<void>

Limits how long a write waits for the system to take more data: when it can take none for milliseconds (the peer is not reading), the write fails with is_timed_out(), possibly after sending part of the data. Each wait counts on its own. 0, the default, waits as long as it takes.

Parameters

  • milliseconds — the longest wait, at most 4294967295 (about 49 days); 0 for none

Returns

  • an Ok result; an error with is_invalid_input() when milliseconds is too large, or an error when the stream is closed

write_timeout

write_timeout(): ulong

Returns the write timeout set_write_timeout set.

Returns

  • the timeout in milliseconds, 0 for none

local_address

local_address(): IoResult<SocketAddress>

Returns this side's address of the connection.

Returns

  • the local address; an error when the stream is closed, or another platform error

peer_address

peer_address(): IoResult<SocketAddress>

Returns the peer's address.

Returns

  • the peer's address; an error when the stream is closed, or another platform error

into_transfer

into_transfer(): SocketTransfer

Moves the connection out of this stream, into a token another thread can take it from with TcpStream.adopt. The stream is closed afterwards (is_open() is false), and a task waiting on it on this worker wakes with an error.

Inside async.run a socket belongs to the worker that uses it; this is how a task hands a connection to a task on another worker, such as one started with async.spawn.

Returns

  • the token; for a closed stream, one that adopt fails on

Example

import async;
import io;

serve(listener: io.TcpListener) {
    var (stream, peer) = listener.accept().value();
    var transfer = stream.into_transfer();
    async.spawn<void>(() => {
        var mine = io.TcpStream.adopt(transfer).value();
        mine.write_all("hello from another worker");
    });
}

close

close(): IoResult<void>

Closes the connection now. Closing a closed stream does nothing.

Returns

  • an Ok result on success or when already closed; the platform error when closing fails

SocketTransfer

[Shared] struct SocketTransfer

A connection on its way from one thread to another: made by TcpStream.into_transfer (or UnixStream.into_transfer), taken by TcpStream.adopt (or UnixStream.adopt, for a Unix domain connection). Unlike a stream, it is thread-safe, so a shared function (a body for async.spawn or Thread.spawn) can capture it and a Channel can carry it. If no one adopts it, the connection is closed when the last reference goes.

Constructor

SocketTransfer()

construct(handle: SocketHandle)

Wraps a socket handle. TcpStream.into_transfer makes these; use it.

Parameters

  • handle — the socket, or an invalid handle for an empty token

UdpSocket

[NotCopyable("owns an operating-system socket and cannot be copied")] struct UdpSocket

A UDP socket: sends and receives datagrams, each delivered whole or not at all, in no guaranteed order.

UdpSocket.bind opens one on a local address (port 0 for any free port). send_to and receive_from name the peer on each call; after connect, send and receive use the connected peer and ignore datagrams from anyone else.

Each receive takes one datagram. A datagram longer than max is truncated to max bytes and the rest is lost, so size max for the largest datagram expected (at most 65507 bytes over IPv4).

Closing: the destructor closes the socket when the last reference goes; close() closes it earlier and reports errors.

Example

import io;

var socket = io.UdpSocket.bind(io.SocketAddress.parse("0.0.0.0:9000").value()).value();
var buffer = Array<u8>();
var (n, from) = socket.receive_from(buffer, 65507).value();
socket.send_to(buffer, from);   # echo it back

Unix domain sockets

Unix domain sockets: UnixListener accepts connections on a path in the file system, UnixStream is one connection, and UnixDatagram sends and receives datagrams.

They work like TcpListener, TcpStream and UdpSocket, for processes on the same machine: a path names the socket instead of an IP address and a port. Linux, macOS and Windows (10 version 1803 and later) all have the stream sockets; UnixDatagram is Linux and macOS only.

Binding creates a socket file at the path, and closing the listener does not remove it: remove it with File.remove when the server is done, and before binding again, since binding to a path that exists fails with is_address_in_use().

Source: runtime/io/unix.pep

UnixListener

[NotCopyable("owns an operating-system socket and cannot be copied")] struct UnixListener

A Unix domain socket that listens for connections on a path.

UnixListener.bind creates the socket file and listens on it; each accept() waits for the next connection and returns it as a UnixStream.

Closing: the destructor closes the socket when the last reference goes; close() closes it earlier and reports errors. Neither removes the socket file. Every operation on a closed listener fails with an error no IoError predicate identifies (EBADF on POSIX, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE on Windows).

See also

  • UnixStream

Example

import io;

var path = io.Directory.temp().join("server.sock");
io.File.remove(path);   # left over from an earlier run
var listener = io.UnixListener.bind(path).value();
while (true) {
    var stream = listener.accept().value();
    stream.write_all("hello");
}

SharedUnixListener

[Shared] struct SharedUnixListener

A Unix domain listening socket that any thread can accept connections on: the thread-safe counterpart of UnixListener, as SharedTcpListener is of TcpListener. Each connection goes to one of the threads waiting in accept, and the stream it returns belongs to that thread.

A shared function may capture it. There is no close(), since another thread may be waiting on it: the socket closes when the last reference goes. The socket file stays.

See also

  • UnixListener

Example

import async;
import io;

main(): int {
    async.run(() => {
        var listener = io.SharedUnixListener.bind(io.Path("/tmp/server.sock")).value();
        async.spawn_on_each_worker(() => {
            while (true) {
                var accepted = listener.accept();
                if (accepted.is_err()) {
                    return;
                }
                accepted.value().write_all("hello");
            }
        });
    });
    return 0;
}

UnixStream

[NotCopyable("owns an operating-system socket and cannot be copied")] struct UnixStream

A Unix domain stream connection: a reliable, ordered stream of bytes in both directions between two processes (or threads) on this machine.

Get one from UnixStream.connect or UnixListener.accept. Reading and writing work exactly as on a TcpStream: read appends what has arrived and returns 0 once the peer has closed its side, write may send part of the data, and read_exact and write_all loop until done. Sending never raises SIGPIPE; writing to a connection the peer has closed fails with is_connection_reset() (or a broken-pipe error no predicate matches, on some systems).

Closing: the destructor closes the socket when the last reference goes; close() closes it earlier and reports errors. Every operation on a closed stream fails with an error no IoError predicate identifies.

See also

  • UnixListener

Example

import io;

var stream = io.UnixStream.connect(io.Path("/tmp/server.sock")).value();
stream.write_all("ping");
var reply = Array<u8>();
stream.read_exact(reply, 4).value();

UnixDatagram

[Target(OS(Linux) || OS(Mac))] [NotCopyable("owns an operating-system socket and cannot be copied")] struct UnixDatagram

A Unix domain datagram socket (SOCK_DGRAM on AF_UNIX): like a UdpSocket for processes on the same machine, with a path in place of an address. Linux and macOS only; Windows has no Unix datagram sockets.

Each send_to delivers one whole datagram, in order, and the system never drops one silently. While the receiver's queue is full, a send waits on Linux; on macOS it fails at once with the platform's "No buffer space available" (ENOBUFS) and sends nothing, so try again later. UnixDatagram.bind creates a socket file at a path, which closing does not remove (as for UnixListener); UnixDatagram.unbound makes a socket that can send but has no path for replies; UnixDatagram.pair makes two connected sockets.

Closing: the destructor closes the socket when the last reference goes; close() closes it earlier and reports errors. Every operation on a closed socket fails with an error no IoError predicate identifies (EBADF).

See also

  • UdpSocket
  • UnixStream

Example

import io;

var path = io.Directory.temp().join("events.sock");
io.File.remove(path);   # left over from an earlier run
var server = io.UnixDatagram.bind(path).value();
var client = io.UnixDatagram.unbound().value();
client.send_to("ping".bytes(), path);
var buffer = Array<u8>();
var (n, from) = server.receive_from(buffer, 1024).value();   # 4, an empty path

Streams in memory

ByteReader and ByteWriter: a Reader over bytes already in memory, and a Writer that collects what is written into memory, for code that takes a stream when the data is in an array.

Source: runtime/io/memory.pep

ByteReader

struct ByteReader

A Reader over an array of bytes: each read takes the next bytes of the array, and the stream ends after its last byte.

The reader keeps a reference to the array and does not copy it; changing the array while reading changes what is read.

Example

import io;

var data = "one\ntwo\n".bytes();
var count = 0;
for (var line in io.ByteReader(data).lines()) {
    count += 1;
}
assert(count == 2, "two lines");
